adjustments.change: Add an explicit precedence clause so that when the already-observed source still offers the remaining instance, returning to it overrides any general locate-phase widening rule (including one that prefers untried destinations over recently observed ones); keep the source-identification condition, the immediate post-placement return, the no-re-sweep and widen-only-if-source-empty clauses, and the locate-take-deliver/completion boundary unchanged.
adjustments.reason: The direction is supported by the current batch: in `G3`, after placing book 1 at desk 1 (`P6:8`) the actor had already seen book 2 on bed 1 (`P6:5`) yet spent about thirty steps sweeping shelf 1/shelf 2/sidetable 1/drawer 1/drawer 2 before returning to bed 1 (`P6:39`) to take book 2 (`P6:43`), whereas the successful `P7` counterpart placed creditcard 2 and returned directly to the same source desk 1 (`P7:6`) to take creditcard 3 (`P7:9`), finishing successfully in 9 total steps. The retained completion boundary agrees with `M5`, which found same-receptacle two-instance delivery preserved in successful two-object runs and the sole regression arising from splitting instances across containers rather than from retrieval routing. Coordination is the actual implemented change: `M6` records that the widening rule constrains which destinations to avoid, and `P3` shows the retrieval and widening phases share the same locate window, so without an explicit precedence the general untried-destination rule could label the just-observed source a stall and block the required return. The clause is bounded to the case where the source still offers the instance, so it does not suppress widening when the source is exhausted.
